_what: THE single definition of the compat-envelope scorecard shape. Producers and guards derive from THIS; nothing restates a column list inline.
_why: Measured at origin/main 2026-08-07: five emitters declared FIVE DISTINCT column
lists and shared none. Even the two 36-column ones were different shapes. That is
the hardcoded-list-of-a-growing-set defect in schema form, and it is silent: the
row gets written, parses fine, and is misread by index later.
The shape is CORE + PER-VARIANT EXTENSIONS. Core order is load-bearing: a variant
appends its extras AFTER the full core, so a reader that knows only the core can
still index every core column correctly in any variant.
_generated_from: derived once from origin/main scorecard headers, then authoritative. check_emitter_schema.py enforces both directions, so this file cannot silently drift from the CSVs nor they from it.

_known_violation.reverie-scorecard.csv: TWO violations of the core-prefix rule, both measured at origin/main 2026-08-07: (1) omits the core column 'stdout_parity'; (2) inserts its extra 'tool_count_parity' at index 14, MID-CORE, rather than after the core. Either alone breaks core-position indexing for this variant. This is also why collect-reverie-compat.rs misaligns when it appends into the 33-column canonical scorecard (its DEFAULT --csv target): the columns disagree in content AND order, not merely in count. Recorded, not blessed. Fixing needs the emitter, currently owned by hermit-w7.

_core_prefix_rule: A variant SHOULD be its core columns in core order, then its extras. That is what lets a reader who knows only the core index every core column correctly in any variant. `core_prefix_safe` records whether each variant actually obeys it; the checker reports a violation rather than silently accepting it.

unimplemented_comparisons._what: Comparisons the strict standard names that NOTHING CURRENTLY PERFORMS. Declared here so a cell cannot appear to satisfy one, and so the gap is a fact in the schema rather than folklore.
_why: Measured at origin/main 2026-08-07 across all 4 scorecards, 2290 rows.
The strict standard is stdout + INFO log + stack + heap. Mapping each to the
column that would carry it: stdout -> stdout_parity (0 of 2278 non-blank),
INFO log -> compared_log_messages (6 of 2290), stack -> stack_hash (6 of 624),
heap -> heap_hash (6 of 624). Before those 6 rows landed, ALL FOUR were zero.
A cell claiming strict was claiming four comparisons of which none were
recorded -- a green against an empty check, not a weak green.
A column blank on every row also cannot be mutation-tested: there is nothing
to plant a wrong value in. And check_cell_comparison.py, which exists to catch
a verdict carrying no reference, reports 0 of 0 verdicts and exits 0 -- it is
vacuous for exactly this reason. A passing guard there means nothing today.

columns_with_no_producer.stdout_parity: 0 of 2278 rows non-blank. THE COLUMN NOW HAS A WRITER BUT STILL NO PRODUCTION PRODUCER, and the distinction is the whole point of leaving it declared here. strict_verdict.scorecard_fields() writes stdout_parity as of 2026-08-07 (before that it accepted a stdout verdict, used it to compose the tier, and dropped it). But NOTHING IN A COLLECTOR CALLS scorecard_fields -- its only callers are its own tests -- so no published row gains a value. Removing this entry now would assert a producer that no pipeline invokes. Delete it when a collector calls it, not before.
columns_with_no_producer.ref_output_hash: 0 of 2290 rows non-blank. Without it a recorded stdout verdict has no reference to re-check.
columns_with_no_producer.parity_comparator: 0 of 2290 rows non-blank. No row states which comparator produced its parity verdict.
columns_with_no_producer.parity_tier: 0 of 2290 rows non-blank. No row states the tier its parity verdict was earned at.
columns_with_no_producer.detlog_parity: NEW COLUMN, added 2026-08-07. The detlog producer already existed and already emitted this exact key from strict_verdict.scorecard_fields(); until now the schema had nowhere to put it, so the verdict was computed and discarded. The column now exists; the same unwired-caller caveat as stdout_parity applies, so it stays declared and must remain blank.
columns_with_no_producer.exit_code_parity: NEW COLUMN, added 2026-08-07. No producer computes an exit-code comparison. scorecard_fields() accepts an `exit_code` verdict so a future producer has a typed field to return instead of inventing a second convention, but nothing supplies one.
columns_with_no_producer.oracle_verdict: NEW COLUMN, added 2026-08-07. No producer computes an oracle verdict. compat-envelope/absolute-oracles.csv exists but nothing joins it to a scorecard row.

unimplemented_comparisons._rule: A column listed in columns_with_no_producer MUST be blank on every row. The moment a real producer exists, remove it from this list IN THE SAME CHANGE that adds the producer -- check_unimplemented_comparisons.py refuses a non-blank value in a declared-unimplemented column, so the declaration cannot rot into a lie in either direction.  SECOND HALF OF THE RULE, added 2026-08-07 with the exit_code_parity / detlog_parity / oracle_verdict columns: check_cell_comparison.py polices only VERDICT_COLUMNS = (stdout_parity, tool_count_parity) and pairs them with the single REFERENCE_COLUMN ref_output_hash. The three new columns are deliberately NOT added to VERDICT_COLUMNS, because ref_output_hash is the wrong operand for them: a detlog verdict's reference is the run1/run2 detlog digest, and an oracle verdict's is the oracle identity -- demanding an OUTPUT hash beside either would force a producer to record a reference it did not compare against, which is a fabricated binding, not a check. So the coupling requirement is: WHOEVER ADDS A PRODUCER FOR ONE OF THESE COLUMNS MUST, IN THE SAME CHANGE, NAME ITS OWN REFERENCE COLUMN AND TEACH check_cell_comparison.py THE (verdict, reference) PAIR -- not reuse ref_output_hash. Until then the columns are held blank by this list, which is what keeps the gap closed in the interim.
unimplemented_comparisons._representability_note: comparisons_with_no_column is EMPTY as of 2026-08-07: exit_code, detlog and oracle gained exit_code_parity / detlog_parity / oracle_verdict. That closes ABSENT CAPACITY only. Each moved into columns_with_no_producer, which is a strictly weaker defect but still a defect: there is now somewhere to write, and still nothing writing. Adding a column is not adding a measurement, and the count of declared-unimplemented comparisons deliberately did not drop when the columns landed.
